He's almost 3, and he wants to play the PS4, but his hands are too small and there's too many buttons for him. I can tell him "push the blue button." but he has trouble doing that while pushing other buttons and looking at the screen. He also instinctively holds both analog sticks straight up for some reason so whatever game he plays he's walking forward looking straight up.

SNES and Genesis might not be too complicated for him, but I think 2 buttons and a DPad (plus start and select) might be easier for him, as well as the smaller size.

Been sitting here thinking about how much of a roller coaster my taste for alcohol has been, now I'm curious as to everyone else's preferences over the years.

I started off with JD as my drink of choice when I was but a young lad, but after an eventful night I was turned off of whiskey for a while (think 2 fingers left of a 1.75L between two friends). To replace my JD I turned to Rum, mostly Bacardi, and then shifted more towards the tequila scene after a while....but that eventually grew a little tiring and I then started drinking cranberry-vodka's (skull vodka being the epitome of my vodka enjoyment), loved them...can't stand them any more for some reason. After my CranVod phase I was heavily into dirty martini's with copious amounts of vermouth...that eventually led me down a path of trying out more upper-shelf Gins which in turn led to drinking Gin & Tonics. I then tried to pick up some dark rum, but didn't like it at all. Lately I've come back to trying out grocery store top shelf whiskey's...where I ran into ryes...now my life feels incomplete if I have no rye in the house...preferably Basil Hayden's, though I am still somewhat new to the whole rye scene. Who knows where I'll go from here, today I picked up a bottle of Knob Creek Single Barrel bourbon to give it a whirl, but I'm already wishing I had grabbed new rye to try instead.

Anyone else care to share their thoughts or preferences over the years?
My taste for spirits over the years

My drinking career was influenced by my father, who enjoyed his bourbon. He was not adventuresome in his selection, so I was not exposed to much variety. When I entered the military at age 17, I decided that I was a scotch drinker, mostly on the advice of one "Lynyrd Skynyrd", who referenced a "Johnny Walker Red" in one of their ditties. I choked down as much of this vile concoction as I could stand. Thankfully, this phase passed quickly, before much brain damage had occurred. Or that's what I tell myself. Tequila came next, and, like yourself, an eventful night made the cactus juice a non starter for a decade or so. Irish, bourbon, and scotch whiskies of the grocery store variety got me through the next few decades, with Jamesons, Makers, and JW Black being staples. There was a detour into gin, with Red Bull getting mixed with several cases of Bombay Sapphire (a very nice combo). Now, in the autumn of life, I try as many different tastes as I can, as long as it's whiskey. Most recently, I tried a fine Irish, a 15 year old Redbreast, and I plan on purchasing a good supply, as it is truly one of the best tastes of my life. Oh and then there's Fireball, when I need to get the wife wound up.
